That points to a self-referencing or very deeply nested payload. After each restart the worker resumes at the same committed offset 246773 and crashes on the same message again, which produces the CrashLoopBackOff. The consumer is stuck, so catalog.updates lag grows (search-api warnings show it climbing from 1344 to 10409). No deploy shows up in the logs, and the crashes are on the same version, v4.5.8. The other services log no errors.
An unbounded recursion bug in expandReferences in v4.5.8 is possible. But the worker ran fine on this version until it hit one specific message, and no deploy appears in the logs.

verdict.recommendedAction: Skip msg-195727 (offset 246773) or move it to a dead-letter queue, for example by committing the offset past it, so index-worker can catch up. Then add a depth limit or cycle detection to expandReferences, catch errors for each message and send failed messages to the dead-letter queue, and look into why the producer published a message with circular references.
